lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Stillness. Not silence — stillness. The air doesn't move. Dust hangs motionless. A single drop of water clings to a stone lip and doesn't fall.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: He stops breathing. Not out of fear. Out of recognition. This is what he does — he sits with old things and tries to keep them from disappearing. This place understands that.

lines.speaker: Zi
lines.lens: No air current. Particles suspended. The water droplet has been there long enough to leave a mineral stain, but it hasn't fallen. Time is moving differently here. Or it isn't moving at all.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: Lyenne. Time and patience. The god of the long view.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The shrine is a flat stone, worn smooth by centuries or by intention — it's impossible to tell. On its surface, faint lines trace patterns that could be writing or could be the natural record of age itself. The difference may not matter here.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: This is what preservation feels like. Not holding on. Just... not rushing.
lines.monologue: He sits down next to the stone without deciding to. His body recognized what this was before his mind did. A place where things are allowed to take as long as they take.

lines.speaker: Caelan
lines.text: It feels like standing at the edge of something.
lines.monologue: Not a cliff. A pause. The longest pause he's ever felt. Like the moment before a held breath releases, stretched out until it becomes a place.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The stillness holds. It doesn't press or pull. It simply offers the rarest thing: enough time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Something is placed on the smooth stone. Nothing happens. And then, slowly, something does: the faint lines on the surface shift, and for a moment the stone shows what it looked like a hundred years ago, and a hundred years before that, and before that — layers of time, visible all at once, like rings in a cut tree. Then it settles back to now.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.monologue: He's crying. Quietly. Not from sadness. From the relief of seeing that the things he spends his life trying to save were never really gone. They're just further back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The water droplet falls. Time resumes its ordinary pace, carrying them forward the way it always has — gently, without asking permission.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They leave the stillness. It doesn't end — they simply step out of it, back into the current of ordinary time.

lines.speaker: Lex
lines.text: I'd like to come back here.
lines.monologue: He knows he probably won't. But the wanting matters. Lyenne would understand that. Wanting is just patience that hasn't found its way yet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, the water droplet still hasn't fallen. It will wait.
